stops.note: Old Javanese inscriptions record jong for large ocean-going ships; an older idea that the word came from Chinese chuán 'boat' fits the sounds poorly
Tomé Pires, writing his Suma Oriental in Portuguese Malacca around 1512-15, describes the great Javanese juncos trading there
English traders in Asia took it from the Portuguese; the Keying, a Chinese junk that sailed to London in 1848, drew huge crowds (junk 'rubbish' is an unrelated word)

current_meaning: a flat-bottomed Chinese sailing ship with battened sails
